candidates.title: Maersk revises intermodal fuel fees in Italy
candidates.excerpt: Maersk will revise its Intermodal Fuel Fee percentages for truck and RCO movements in Italy. The new levels apply equally to export and import inland services. The revised rates will apply from a price calculation date of 1 October 2026 for non-FMC-regulated shipments. For FMC-regulated shipments, they will take effect from a price calculation date of 24 October 2026. The new percentages will replace the previously announced levels. Maersk will review the charges monthly in response to developments in fuel and energy markets.

The analysis comes as potash has become a political issue. candidates.excerpt: Trains Turntable: Commentary from Association of American Railroads CEO Ian Jefferies For 10 years, See Tracks? Think Train Week has reminded Americans of a simple but essential fact: railroad tracks are not places to take chances with your safety. This annual campaign has helped raise awareness about the dangers for drivers and pedestrians around railroad tracks and crossings. But as we mark its 10th anniversary, we should also recognize that the most effective way to prevent collisions at highway-rail crossings is to eliminate the crossing altogether. That is why Congress should provide sustained, robust funding for the Railroad Crossing Elimination (RCE) Grant Program. Every one of the nation’s 200,000 grade crossings presents a potential point of conflict between trains, vehicles, and pedestrians. candidates.excerpt: Germany’s Offen Group is looking to return to containership newbuildings after more than a decade away, with the Hamburg tonnage provider linked to up to four ships at China’s Guangzhou Shipyard International. Shipbroking and market sources have Offen in discussions with the CSSC-controlled yard for two firm plus two optional 7,000 teu vessels, with delivery slots pencilled in for 2030. The company’s own fleet pages describe Offen as Germany’s largest non-operating containership owner, managing more than 40 ships across panamax, post-panamax and super-post-panamax sizes. Two other MSC vessels MSC Florentina and the MSC Turin III also diverted to the vicinity of the MSC Hermes III that appeared to be adrift around 300 km east of Vietnam.
